title: Unoccupied Metro Line 3 Car Derails at Ticomán Workshop; Metro Blames Rain-Softened Ground
detail: The fifth car of a Metro Line 3 train derailed by about one meter from the tracks at 12:06 p.m. on August 14 while performing maneuvers at the Ticomán maintenance workshop in Gustavo A. Madero, in the rail interchange area rather than passenger service. The train was unoccupied and no injuries were reported. Metro director Adrián Ruvalcaba said initial analysis pointed to 'probable ground condition impact from geological faults and soil softening due to the current rain season,' and crews carried out preventive rail realignment and ballast compaction. Line 3 (Indios Verdes–Universidad) continued normal passenger operation throughout, with no service disruption.

media.caption: An unoccupied Metro Line 3 car derailed at the Ticomán workshop; officials cited rain-softened ground

title: CDMX Congress Approves Electoral Reform Capping Regidor Seats and State Legislature Budgets
detail: The Congreso CDMX approved a minuta implementing the federal electoral reform on August 14 by a vote of 49 in favor, 16 against, and no abstentions. The reform limits the number of municipal regidurías, caps state congress budgets at a fixed share of public spending, and sets salary ceilings for electoral officials. Legislators supporting the measure framed it as part of a 'republican austerity' push to end privileges in electoral bureaucracy and redirect public resources; opposition lawmakers warned of impacts on legislative staffing and local budgets.
